parts.q: Find an equation of the line containing the point \((4,-6)\) whose \(x\)-intercept is \(1\).
parts.a: The \(x\)-intercept is the point \((1,0)\). The slope is \(m = \dfrac{0-(-6)}{1-4} = -2\), so \(y = -2(x-1) = -2x + 2\).

parts.q: Find an equation of the line whose \(x\)-intercept is \(-5\) and whose \(y\)-intercept is \(8\).
parts.a: The points are \((-5,0)\) and \((0,8)\). The slope is \(m = \dfrac{8-0}{0-(-5)} = \dfrac{8}{5}\) and the \(y\)-intercept is \(8\), so \(y = \dfrac{8}{5}x + 8\).
